notes: Renders a `<div role="slider">` rather than an `<input type="range">`. The native range input cannot be styled into a two-part track-and-fill without pseudo-element hacks that differ per browser, which the unstyled model cannot accept. The cost used to be that every keyboard and pointer behaviour had to be reimplemented and none of it was generated; the `range` block closed that.

aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuenow are generated from the state's min, max and current value. aria-valuenow reports the SNAPPED value, not the one handed in — a controlled value may arrive off-step or out of range, and drawing the thumb at one number while announcing another is worse than either. aria-valuetext is still NOT generated: the contract says some ranges need text instead of a bare number and has no way to supply it.

The keyboard and the drag are executed by `useRangeControl` from `@ds/react/behavior`, an imported dependency rather than copied code. The `track` part named by the contract carries a ref, because a pointer position means nothing until something says which box it is measured against.

The fill's length and the thumb's offset are published as `--ds-fraction` on the root: one number, 0..1, already clamped and snapped. This is the first time a generated component hands CSS a computed value. It is not a layout declaration and does not belong in the `paints` model — turning a fraction into a percentage is styling, computing the fraction is not — but it does mean `--ds-fraction` is a name this backend invented and nothing in the contract system defines.
`dragging` is `control: internal`: no prop can set it, and it reaches the DOM only as `data-ds-state-dragging` for styling.

Pointer capture is attempted and its failure is swallowed. It throws for any pointerId the browser has no active pointer for, which is every synthesised event — a test harness, an automation driver, an assistive tool that clicks. Losing capture degrades the drag once the pointer leaves the element; letting the exception out would kill the press entirely.
